text:
maria: Heads-up — after flipping to per-channel calibration for FP8 kernels I’m seeing a measurable perf regression in the runtime profiling. Attaching the short summary below, can folks who touched calibration/batching take a look? :eyes:

maria: PROFILE SNAPSHOT:
```
baseline (FP8 per-tensor, batch=8): 13.1k toks/s, p50=42ms, p95=115ms
per-channel FP8 (same infra): 9.0k toks/s, p50=58ms, p95=210ms  <-- ~ -31% throughput
INT8 baseline (for reference): 12.0k toks/s
KV-cache hit ratio dropped ~3.2% after the new scales landed
```

maria: Notes: the regression shows up more for batch sizes <=8, and for the long-tail documents (lots of rare tokens). I suspect per-channel scale layout is causing noisy kernel choices and more KV-store churn.

noah: Can you paste the calibration config you used? sample composition + sample size matters a lot here.

maria: Sure — we used the default "corpus-wide" sampler with 10k sequences, per-channel mode, include-docs-longer-than=all. Config fragment:
```
{"mode":"per-channel","sample_size":10000,"max_seq":2048,"per_doc_cap":0}
```

sam: Quick theory: per-channel increases quant metadata per-row, which on our kernel selector triggers a different kernel path (vector width changes) and also invalidates some cache-friendly packing. If the sampler included many hotkey-heavy docs, the per-channel scales will be dominated by outliers and force conservative kernels.

lina: On quality side, eval on our 2k holdout shows negligible quality gain (delta LL = +0.003) but perf hit is big. So if we get only tiny quality benefit, not worth 30% drop.

jon: Two immediate experiments: 1) clip outlier contribution (exclude top X percentile tokens per-channel) 2) cap per-doc token contribution so a single long doc can’t dominate scales.

sam: Also try mixed strategy: per-channel for top 4 layers (or attention/FFN split) and per-tensor elsewhere. That keeps most of the representational gains but limits kernel path divergence.

maria: Agree. Proposing an AB matrix:
- A: per-tensor (baseline)
- B: per-channel full corpus
- C: per-channel with exclude-top-0.5pct outliers
- D: mixed (per-channel top-4 layers, per-tensor others)
Measure: tokens/s, p95 latency, KV-hit, eval LL on 2k set.

noah: I can run A/B/C today on dev cluster. Quick command I’ll use:
```
./calib-run --mode per-channel --sample-size 10000 --exclude-top 0.005 --per-layer-mask "0-3" --out results.json
```

ci-bot: build/test pipeline finished for branch calibrate/2026-perchannel. No regressions in unit tests.

lina: Small suggestion on sampling: stratify by doc length and by top-k token frequency buckets (hotkeys vs tail). If sampling is uniform by doc, hotkey docs can overweight rare tokens.

sam: +1 to stratified sampling. Another low-cost hack: when computing per-channel scales, use median-of-means across shards (reduces sensitivity to single huge-value shards).

jon: Also watch KV cache layout — if quant table size changes alignment we get extra memcpy and L2 trashing. We should log kernel-selection reason in profiler (e.g., why this kernel chosen: alignment/width/flags) so we can correlate.

maria: Good call. I’ll add a profiler flag to emit kernel-decision trace for these runs.

noah: Starting run B and C now on dev-gpu-01. Will post results here when done. :coffee:

sam: If B shows any sizable quality wins over A, we can try per-channel but with a calibration post-process: 1) compute raw per-channel scales 2) clip per-channel scales at layer-level percentiles 3) re-run a cheap stability pass (small sample) to verify no degredation.

lina: If we end up keeping per-channel only for a subset of layers, we should document which layers and include them in the model metadata so runtime can pick a fast fallback kernel when those layers aren’t present.

maria: TL;DR: we need to decide fast — perf regression affects a few prod routes. Plan: noah runs A/B/C, sam and jon instrument kernel-trace, lina runs eval metrics on the small holdout. Meet tomorrow 10:30 to decide rollout. /cc @sam @jon @lina @noah :face_with_monocle:

noah: results (initial):
```
A (per-tensor): 13.0k toks/s, p95=112ms, KV-hit=92.1%, LL=-1.234
B (per-channel full): 9.1k toks/s, p95=208ms, KV-hit=88.8%, LL=-1.231
C (per-channel excl top0.5%): 12.4k toks/s, p95=118ms, KV-hit=91.6%, LL=-1.233
```

noah: So excluding the top 0.5% of token magnitude in the calibration sample recovers almost all perf and keeps most of the (small) quality improvement.

maria: Amazing, that’s exactly the signal we wanted. Can we add that exclude-top parameter to the default calibrator and make stratified sampling the default for corpora with >1M tokens?

sam: I’ll push a PR for default exclude-top=0.005 + stratified sampler toggle. Will also add kernel-decision logging.

jon: I’ll watch for any KB/pack alignment regressions in eng-runtime after the PR.

lina: I’ll update the docs/NOTES for calibration guidance: recommend per-channel only when sample_size>5k AND exclude-top>=0.5pct OR mixed-layer mask.

maria: Thanks everyone. This is a good pragmatic fix — avoids rolling back per-channel entirely. Follow-up: we should still run a larger eval to confirm across languages. Meeting tomorrow 10:30. :thumbsup:
